text:
maria: FYI Windows CI failing on py3.11/3.10 with SSLCertVerificationError when company root CA is used.

alex: Native Windows runner or WSL?

maria: native hosted agent. Minimal repro: `import redwood; redwood.Client().generate("hi")` -> ssl.SSLCertVerificationError.

sam: do you have SSL_CERT_FILE or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE set?

maria: no, we rely on company certs in Windows store. New hires hit this when running the sample app.

jordan: our async client (httpx) fails too on the same image. Typing bug: AsyncClient stubs lack `__aenter__/__aexit__` so linters complain.

alex: proposal: add `ca_bundle` constructor arg (path/bytes) and `prefer_windows_certs` option; also make TLS verification errors non-retryable by default to avoid retry storms. Add `redwood.util.get_ca_bundle()` helper.

sam: +1, and add a small windows-latest CI test that loads a custom cafile. I can help write it.

maria: created PR with fix + docs, CI queued. Assigning to @alex and @sam to land typing + retry change and @jordan to update quickstart docs.

ci-bot: Created PR #1234: "py: add ca_bundle option + windows cert docs"

maria: thanks everyone, this should reduce onboarding friction for Windows users. :raised_hands:
